patch.value: Reduce native list and get latency on large indexed trackers

The orientation latency receipt on a complete 2991-item public tracker copy measured native list p50 731.6 ms versus oracle 445.3 ms, and native get p50 692.6 ms versus oracle 433.7 ms (30 cold processes each, shared 4-CPU host, warm filesystem and oracle derived caches). Investigate selective lookup or validated derived indexes without weakening authoritative read correctness, concurrency, or parity. Keep this optimization separate from the orientation command slice.
Measure the same 30-run commands and retain byte parity, storage integrity and all coverage dimensions.

The final 30-run cold-process receipt on a complete 2991-item public tracker copy measured native list p50 4807.6 ms versus oracle 4000.8 ms, and native get p50 4405.4 ms versus oracle 3715.0 ms. This is a heavily contended shared 4-CPU host with effective nice 15, warm filesystem and oracle derived caches; 1-minute load ranged 20.07 to 44.97. The earlier lower-load 22f7fd0 receipt also showed slower native list/get. Investigate selective lookup or validated derived indexes without weakening authoritative read correctness, concurrency or parity. Retain this optimization as a separate follow-up to the orientation command slice.

The final parser-cleanup release receipt on a complete 2991-item public tracker copy measured 30 cold processes per command/runtime: native list p50 2116.0 ms versus oracle 1269.9 ms, and native get p50 1864.8 ms versus oracle 1118.5 ms. This is a shared 4-CPU host with effective nice 15, warm filesystem and oracle derived caches; sampled 1-minute load ranged 13.84 to 25.64. Earlier completed receipts also showed slower native list/get. Investigate selective lookup or validated derived indexes without weakening authoritative read correctness, concurrency or parity. Keep this optimization separate from the orientation command slice.
